title: triage-thread-quicklog-noor
content:
Quick log for morning console triage (shorthand).

Context: customer-reported slow dashboard tile updates and missing traces in the trace panel. Issue first seen 2026-03-09 evening, escalation last night from CS. I own initial triage this morning before handoff to SRE rotation.

What I checked (fast):
- Confirmed alert: "dashboard-update-latency" fired 3x between 03-09 21:40–22:15 PST.
- Looked at console logs for frontend-service (prod-us-west): spikes in render times ~1200ms at 21:42.
- Query: metrics -> sum(api.response_time_ms{route="/tiles"}) by 1m shows tail at same window.
- Traces: several incomplete spans (missing child spans) in traces for tile-collector; likely dropped by collector due to backpressure.
- Customer sample: cust-acme: session id = f2a3.. logged missing traces and stale tile data.

Repro steps I tried (quick):
1) Load dashboard with timeline filter 24h -> deterministic slowness on first load, subsequent loads okay.
2) curl to /tiles endpoint with sample payload (from customer log) -> response 520ms locally (expected ~120ms) when using same API key.
3) Disabled client-side cache in request -> no improvement, suggests server-side.

Immediate hypotheses:
- Ingest burst to tile-collector causing KV cache churn and blocking requests.
- A recent kernel bump on one node changed epoll behavior? (check infra notes)
- Rate-limiter config for route /tiles possibly misconfigured for burst handling.

Short-term mitigation notes (what I did / can do now):
- Bumped route concurrency limit on prod-us-west router for /tiles from 50 -> 80 (temporary) via console route edit. Kept change for 30m window.
- Added temporary alert annotation for impacted customers (CS notified).
- Created a short-lived canary rule to route 10% of /tiles traffic to a less-loaded pool (pool-archive-2).

Follow-ups (owners + due):
- Deep trace analysis: Priya S. to correlate span drops with collector logs (due 2026-03-12 EOD).
- Infra check: Eli R. to verify node kernel/epoll patches and recent upgrades on prod-us-west (due 2026-03-12 EOD).
- Rate-limit review: me (Noor) to audit rate-limiter configs across regions and propose safe defaults (due 2026-03-13).
- Customer comms: CS ticket JIRA-7892 needs a status update; ask CS to send the workaround (temporary route bump) and ETA for full fix (due 2026-03-12 by noon).

Notes to self (things to capture for postmortem):
- Exact timestamps of dropped spans + node IDs (pull from traces index) -> important for correlating to infra events.
- Whether prefix/KV cache eviction cadence changed after last config push (optimize team may have changed TTLs).
- Record the effect of temporary concurrency bump on latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for next 1h window.

Open questions / TODOs (brainstorm fragments):
- Is there a known regression in the serving runtime that could manifest as missing child spans? Check recent PRs to runtime around batching/kv-cache.
- If collector is backpressuring, do we have adaptive shedding or should we add early-return in tile assembly to avoid full request stalls?
- Should we consider adding an internal low-overhead health ping for collectors to detect load earlier?

Quick commands I used (save for next time):
- metrics query (promql): sum(rate(api_response_time_ms_sum{route="/tiles"}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_response_time_ms_count{route="/tiles"}[5m]))
- traces search: service:tile-collector span.name:assemble* | filter duration>300ms | group_by node.id
- logs: resource.type="k8s_container" AND labels.k8s-pod=frontend-service AND severity>=ERROR

Slack / comms to send:
- @cs: "Bumped concurrency for /tiles in prod-us-west and routed 10% traffic to pool-archive-2. Monitoring p95. Will update within 1h with more data."
- @eng-sre: "Assigning Priya for trace correlation and Eli for infra kernel check. See JIRA-7892."

Finish checklist before handoff to SRE rotation (if time):
- [ ] Capture timeline of p95/p99 before and after concurrency bump (10m window).
- [ ] Export sample incomplete trace IDs and attach to JIRA-7892.
- [ ] Confirm canary routing is healthy and remove if it worsens latencies.

Random aside (personal): remember to push the quick script that automates trace-export for Handoff (spent 30m yesterday; finish it tomorrow).

End of morning quicklog. Keep this doc short and update in place; will copy into the formal incident doc if we escalate to sev2.
